newsitem.title: USA: Delta, Southwest post higher profits despite fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: Delta, Southwest post higher profits despite fuel costs.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc. and Southwest Airlines Co. reported strong profits for the latest quarter Thursday despite higher jet fuel costs, becoming the latest major airlines to post solid results.

Delta, the nation's third largest carrier, posted net income of $189 million, or $2.52 a share, for its third quarter, compared with a net loss of $276 million, or $5.77 a share, a year earlier, when it took a big charge.
Southwest said its first-quarter net income climbed 54 percent to $50.9 million, or 34 cents a share, from $33 million, or 22 cents a share.
Investors, however, had totally different reactions to the quarterly earnings reports.

Delta's stock fell $1.375 to $96.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange, even though its per-share earnings of $2.52 were far better than Wall Street estimates of $2.14, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
But Southwest, whose per-share earnings of 34 cents were 11 cents better than analysts' estimates, added $1.50 to $26.625 on the NYSE, where it was one of the most active issues.

The strong earnings reports followed similar strong performances by United Airlines, American Airlines, Continental Airlines and Northwest Airlines, which all reported earnings above Wall Street estimates on Tuesday.

Delta's latest results included charges of $52 million related to realignment of trans-Atlantic operations. The year-ago quarter included charges of $556 million, primarily due to writeoffs related to its fleet of older Lockheed L-1011 jetliners.

The Atlanta-based airline said revenues rose to $3.4 billion from $3.0 billion. The gain came on an 11 percent increase in passenger traffic, a 3 percent gain in average fare yields and an 84 percent improvement in other revenues.
Delta's operating income was $346 million in the current quarter compared with an operating loss of $387 million a year earlier.
Excluding a fuel expense increase of 22 percent, operating costs declined slightly compared with the year-ago quarter, Delta said.
Dallas-based Southwest said revenues rose 15 percent to $887.1 million from $772.5 million while operating income grew 52 percent to $87.2 million from $57.4 million.
The company said that, excluding fuel, its operating costs per available seat mile were essentially unchanged.
"We were extremely pleased with our first quarter 1997 unit cost performance," Chairman Herbert Kelleher said in a statement.
